title: Rights and Responsibilities: Access, Spend, and Vendor Stewardship Playbook
author: Asha Menon
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s cross‑company approach to access and permissions, change governance, data handling, procurement & expense authorization, vendor onboarding and travel governance. It consolidates rights, responsibilities, and repeatable workflows so teams can move quickly while preserving security, financial controls, and compliance.

Audience:
- People managers, finance approvers, information security, IT and SRE staff, procurement/operations partners, and individual contributors requesting access or purchases.

Principles (high level):
- Least privilege by default: grant the minimal set of permissions to do the job, with time‑bound approvals for elevated access.
- Clear separation of duties: authorization, procurement, and technical approvals are distinct and auditable.
- Risk‑based flexibility: low‑risk purchases follow a lightweight flow; high‑risk or high‑value actions require additional approvals and SRE/security review.
- Reuse and standardization: preferred vendors, templates, and default SKU choices reduce cycle time and vendor sprawl.
- Observable decisions: maintain an audit trail for all access grants, change approvals, and vendor contracts.

Scope:
- Applies to all employees, contractors, and vendors who provision access, request purchases, or handle Redwood data.
- Excludes personal purchases not reimbursed by Redwood (subject to People Ops travel policy).

Definitions (quick):
- Requester: person who initiates an access or procurement request.
- Approver: manager or designated budget owner who signs off on spend or role changes.
- Steward: team owner responsible for ongoing entitlement reviews, vendor performance, and contract compliance.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Line Manager: validate business need, ensure least privilege, and approve initial access and expense requests (up to delegated threshold).
- Budget Owner/Finance Approver: confirm budget, cost center, and compliance with purchasing policy; approve spend above delegated threshold.
- Security Owner (InfoSec): review high‑privilege access (>90 days, production systems) and vendor security posture for new integrations.
- Procurement / Vendor Manager: lead contract negotiation for new vendors, track insurance and SLAs, own master agreements.
- Requester: provide accuracy in request form, attach justification and expected duration.

Access & Permissions — Standard Workflow:
1) Request: Requester files a request via the Access Portal with: identity (email), resource, role (least privilege), justification, requested duration, and business owner.
2) Manager approval: Line Manager approves or rejects within 3 business days.
3) Security review trigger: If role is production admin, or requires network changes, an automated flag sends request to InfoSec for security review within 48 hours.
4) Provisioning: Upon approvals, the infra automation applies RBAC changes. Ticket must include change id and expiration timestamp.
5) Recertification: Stewards run quarterly entitlement reviews; any stale grants >30 days past end date will be flagged for removal.

Access request form template (copy into Access Portal):
- Requester: [name, email]
- Team: [team name]
- Resource: [service/console/DB/table]
- Role level: [read | write | admin]
- Justification: [business reason]
- Duration: [1 week | 1 month | permanent (rare)]
- Manager approver: [name]
- Security exceptions: [yes/no & explanation]

Change Management (applies to infra, runtime, and configuration changes):
- Change categories:
  - Minor: nonproduction tweaks, low blast radius, pre‑approved automation (no change window required).
  - Standard: planned changes with known rollback, require change ticket and scheduled CR window.
  - Major: production impacting, new dependencies, schema migrations, or multi‑service rollouts — requires stakeholder signoff, rollbacks, and runbook.

Change request process (numbered steps):
1) Create a change request in the Change Tracker with scope, rollback plan, owner, and test plan.
2) Impact assessment: include SLOs affected, estimated downtime, and runbook contact.
3) Approval chain: team lead -> platform SRE -> Product owner (for user‑facing changes) -> Security (if secrets/keys are changed). Approvals must be recorded in Change Tracker.
4) Schedule: Changes to production occur only in approved windows unless emergency.
5) Execute & observe: runbook owner performs deployment, monitors key metrics for 30 minutes post‑deploy.
6) Post‑change review: within 3 business days record outcome and lessons learned. If incidents occurred, attach incident review.

Data classification & handling:
- Classification levels: PUBLIC | INTERNAL | CONFIDENTIAL | RESTRICTED
- Handling rules (summary):
  - PUBLIC: no restrictions, may be published externally.
  - INTERNAL: company internal, stored on internal services, access limited to employees.
  - CONFIDENTIAL: PII, customer data, invoices — encryption at rest and in transit; store in approved systems.
  - RESTRICTED: regulated data (HIPAA, financial records) — only on Private deployments, strict KMS controls, and contract-level protections.

Table: Storage & Encryption Matrix (text table)
| Classification | Allowed Storage | Encryption at Rest | Extra Controls |
| PUBLIC | Public docs site | N/A | Public review |
| INTERNAL | Redwood internal drives | AES‑256 | Access limited to employees |
| CONFIDENTIAL | Approved DBs/Secrets Store | AES‑256 + KMS | RBAC, logging, DPI checks |
| RESTRICTED | Private deployments / VPC | AES‑256 + customer KMS | Contract clauses, audit logs, HSM as needed |

Data access request checklist:
- Business justification and retention period
- Approval from data steward and manager
- Data minimization: sample only the fields required
- Audit logging enabled

Procurement & Expense Authorization:
- Delegated thresholds (examples):
  - Up to $1,000: Manager approval (single approver)
  - $1,001–$25,000: Manager + Finance approver
  - $25,001–$250,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement lead
  - > $250,000: Executive sponsor & Legal review

Checklist for purchase requests:
1) Business justification and expected ROI or need
2) Cost center and budget code
3) Preferred vendor or justification for new vendor
4) Security or compliance implications (InfoSec signoff if product touches data)
5) Desired contract term and renewal cadence
6) Invoice and payment method

Expense reimbursement policy (summary):
- Submit expense within 30 days of purchase with receipt attached.
- Per‑diem limits for travel: see Travel policy excerpt below.
- Card use: Company cards should be reconciled weekly; personal cards require manager approval for reimbursement above $500.

Vendor lifecycle: onboarding -> performance -> offboarding
Vendor onboarding checklist (required for new vendors):
- Vendor information sheet: legal name, tax id, contact, product summary
- Security questionnaire completed (standard 3rd party assessment)
- Contract template reviewed by Legal and Procurement (inc. SLA, IP, indemnity, termination clauses)
- Insurance certificates collected where applicable
- Data handling annex if the vendor will process REDWOOD data
- Finance setup: W9/W8, payment terms, initial PO (if required)
- Operational contact and escalation path

Vendor performance & review cadence:
- Quarterly reviews for strategic vendors (> $50k/yr) covering SLAs, uptime, cost, and roadmap alignment.
- Annual security revalidation for any vendor with CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data access.

Vendor offboarding steps:
1) Terminate access (keys, accounts) within 2 business days of contract end.
2) Revoke secrets and rotate any shared credentials.
3) Ensure data deletion or return per contract; record certificate of deletion.
4) Close purchase orders and document final invoices.

Travel policy (key points):
- Purpose: enable business travel while controlling cost and minimizing risk.
- Booking: Use approved corporate travel portal for flights and hotels unless travel is under $500.
- Approval: Manager must approve travel plans and estimated cost prior to booking.
- Per‑diem and receipts: Meals and incidentals covered up to regional per‑diem caps; itemized receipts required for non‑card purchases.
- Safety: Emergency contact and travel insurance process documented on People Ops site.

Templates and forms (location):
- Access request template (Access Portal): /templates/access-request
- Purchase request form (Procurement Portal): /templates/purchase-request
- Vendor onboarding pack: /templates/vendor-onboarding-bundle
- Travel approval form: /templates/travel-approval

Enforcement & escalation:
- Noncompliance with access or procurement policies may trigger revocation of privileges and review by People Ops and Finance.
- Disputes about budget ownership or approvals: escalate to Finance Director.
- Security exceptions may be granted for defined project windows with compensating controls and must be renewed every 30 days.

Monitoring & auditability:
- Automated logs: Access grants, change approvals, purchase orders, and vendor contracts must be logged in centralized systems (Access Portal, Change Tracker, Procurement).
- Reports: Monthly access recertification report to execs; quarterly vendor cost and SLA dashboards for Finance & Procurement.

Appendix: Example purchase flow (mini‑SOP)
1) Requester submits purchase request with quotes and justification in Procurement Portal.
2) Manager approves, attaches cost center.
3) Finance approver checks budget and policy; Procurement assesses vendor.
4) If vendor new or purchase > $25k, Procurement issues PO and Legal reviews contract.
5) Procurement sends approval and PO to vendor; Finance tracks invoice and payment.
